name: Terminal knee extension (band)
summary: A band behind the knee pulls it forward; you press the knee back to fully straight.
setup: Loop a band around a solid anchor in front of you at knee height and around the back of the working knee. Step back until the band is taut with a soft knee, side-on to the phone. Straighten the knee fully against the band, hold a second, soften and repeat.
brief: Loop a band around a solid anchor in front of you and around the back of the working knee. Step back until the band is taut with a soft knee.
why: Side-on, the hip–knee–ankle angle reads the last few degrees of straightening directly, which is exactly the range this move is for.
tempo: Straighten 1 s, hold 1 s, release 2 s.
regression: Lighter band, or hands on a support.
contraindications: A knee that locks or gives way, or pain at the back of the knee under the band.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Hips pushing back
faults.tip: The band should straighten the knee, not fold you at the hip. Keep the hips over the feet.

faults.label: Snapping the knee back
faults.tip: Push into straight under control. Snapping into hyperextension loads the back of the joint.

faults.label: Heel lifting
faults.tip: The heel stays down so the quad does the work rather than the calf.

guide.surface: Any firm floor; the anchor must not move.
guide.stop: Pain behind the knee, or the knee not straightening at all.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the kneecap is tracking straight.

points.t: Straightens fully against the band each rep.
Kneecap points straight ahead, not inward.
Upright — the knee moves, the body does not.
